messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary 'release/2026-03-15-canary' breached abort criteria in us-west-2. healthcheck_fail_rate=12%, 5xx_rate_delta=+7.4% over baseline. Auto-escalation: paging current on-call. AlertID=CER-2468007654
PagerDuty: Paging Maya (oncall) — triggered by threshold breach on canary.
Maya: acknowledged, looking now. pinging metrics and logs.
Maya: looking at the dashboard — canary hosts show continuous 503/502 traces starting 03:12 UTC, not all hosts but consistent across the new pool.
Ravi: I see a surge in response latency as well (p95 went from 120ms to 900ms). Could be a resource regression or kernel path for the new runtime.
Maya: rolling healthcheck logs from one instance: ``ERROR healthcheck: upstream request failed: connection reset by peer``. Also seeing ``kv-cache miss rate up`` in the same samples.
Leo: is this affecting prod traffic or only canary?
Maya: traffic is on routing policy: 5% of requests to canary pool. We already have automatic fallback enabled but SLOs show increased errors for customers routed to that pool. Customer-impact: small percentage of API calls returned 5xx or timeout; some streaming connections dropped.
Ravi: abort criteria met (>=10% HC fail OR 5xx spike >5%) — we should flip the kill-switch. Do we have a quick FF toggle for canary partition?
Maya: yes, flag is `canary_release_v2`. I'm going to flip it. Executing safe disable now.
Maya: ```
# disable canary partition via feature-flag
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/api/toggle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"canary_release_v2","state":"off","reason":"auto-abort CER-2468007654"}'
```
oncall-bot: Command accepted, flag change queued. Auditing request id=ff-req-8891.
Maya: flag change confirmed — routing layer reports canary partition removed, traffic should be drained to stable pool now. Initiating canary rollback job (named rollback/2026-03-15-canary).
ops-bot: rollback pipeline started: job-id rb-2468007662. Rolling back model variant to stable v1.4 on affected hosts.
Ravi: monitoring logs — error rate dropping on canary-backed requests. p95 latency returning toward baseline in us-west-2.
Leo: good. Any customer-visible retries? We should post a short note to status page for transient 5xx in us-west-2.
Maya: agreed — small window between 03:12-03:18 UTC where ~3% of requests for the region errored. No data loss. I'll draft status: "Partial API errors in US-West affecting a subset of traffic; mitigated by rollback; no persistent impact".
PagerDuty: Incident resolved for paging purposes — responders acknowledged. If follow-up needed, create incident ticket.
Ravi: creating post-incident ticket with timeline, logs, and initial hypothesis (kv-cache warming + kernel path regression in compiled runtime). Assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml.
Maya: handing off to Leo for next shift monitoring and blameless follow-up. I'm going to sleep; message me if rollback sees regressions.
Leo: taking handoff. I'll keep an eye on healthchecks for next 2 hours and validate canary pool stays disabled. Also will check if rollback left any stale models in edge caches.
Maya: docs/update: will add replay of the failing traces under CER-2468007654 in the incident ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Ravi: adding suggested remediation steps: add additional pre-deploy KV cache warm-up + stricter canary gating on p95 latency.
oncall-bot: Incident CER-2468007654 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Handoff: Maya -> Leo.
Leo: acknowledged. updating ops-channel with final note and ETA for RCA.
Maya: closing thread here. Good job team. :partyparrot:
